title: How Do Acquisition Brokers Prequalify Buyers? A 2026 Guide
summary: Brokers prequalify buyers by checking funds, motivation, decision-makers, and fit before sharing the CIM. SBA 7(a) requires 10% equity.
body_markdown:
Most business brokers have shared a confidential deal file with a buyer who never made an offer. This guide explains how acquisition brokers prequalify buyers, with a focus on the SBA 7(a) rules that shape buyer financing in 2026.


‍


### How Do Acquisition Brokers Prequalify Buyers? The Short Answer


Acquisition brokers prequalify buyers by checking four things before they share the confidential information memorandum (CIM): financial capacity, motivation, decision authority, and deal fit. The CIM is the detailed sales package with the company's financials, customers, and operations. A sound process runs this screen after the buyer signs a nondisclosure agreement (NDA) and fills out a buyer profile.


Business buyer qualification goes further than a home buyer check. A home buyer mainly needs a mortgage. A business buyer also needs the skills to run the company and a lender willing to underwrite its cash flow.


Financing sits at the center of the screen. In the[BizBuySell Q3 2026 Insight Report](https://www.bizbuysell.com/insight-report/) , 78% of buyers surveyed expect to use SBA financing to complete an acquisition. That is why this guide leans on SBA 7(a) acquisition loan rules.


‍


### Start With the Buyer Profile and NDA


The buyer profile and the NDA work as your front gate. Together they tell you who the buyer is and protect the seller before sensitive details change hands.


A buyer profile is a short form that captures what the buyer wants and what they bring. A useful profile covers these fields:


- **Target industry:** The sectors the buyer will consider and any they rule out.
- **Business size:** The revenue or cash flow range the buyer wants to buy.
- **Geography:** Where the buyer will live and operate, including any plans to relocate.
- **Experience:** The buyer's background in management, the industry, or past ownership.
- **Available capital:** Liquid cash the buyer can put into a deal today.


An NDA is a contract in which the buyer promises to keep deal information private. Get it signed before you reveal the business name, financials, or CIM. Then compare the profile to your listing to decide whether the buyer moves forward.


Florida broker Denise S. Houghtaling, quoted in BizBuySell's Q3 2026 report, gives buyers direct advice. She tells them to "have proof of funds and proof of equity injection, get SBA prequalified, and have a buyer profile."


‍


### Verify Financial Capability Before Anything Else


Brokers in BizBuySell's Q3 2026 survey named SBA funding the most common financing obstacle. It was cited by 38% of brokers, ahead of interest rates at 34%.


Financial capability means the buyer can fund their share, pass the lender's checks, and carry the debt. The three checks below cover cash, guarantors, and deal size.


#### Proof of Funds and Equity Injection


Proof of funds is a recent bank or brokerage statement that shows the buyer has the cash they claim. Equity injection is the buyer's own money that goes into the deal, much like a down payment.


Under[SBA SOP 50 10 8.1](https://www.sba.gov/document/sop-50-10-lender-development-company-loan-programs) , effective October 1, 2026, the 10% equity injection for an initial acquisition cannot be reduced or eliminated. SBA measures that 10% on total project cost, not the purchase price alone. If total project cost is $1.2 million, the buyer needs at least $120,000 in qualifying equity.


A seller note is a loan from the seller to the buyer for part of the price. Under the same SOP, it counts as equity only on full standby. That means no principal or interest payments for the life of the SBA 7(a) loan. Seller debt, other standby debt, and minority equity together can cover no more than half of the required injection.


In the $1.2 million example, those sources top out at $60,000. The rest must come from sources such as cash the buyer did not borrow. Our[SBA acquisition financing guide](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-acquisition-financing-for-business-brokers-2026-guide-to-closing-financed-deals) walks through full deal structures.


#### Credit, Guarantors, and Eligibility


A personal guaranty is a promise to repay the loan from personal assets if the business cannot. SOP 50 10 8.1 sets the SBA's personal guaranty requirement: anyone who owns 20% or more of the borrower must give an unlimited full guaranty.


The lender must also collect a personal financial statement from every guarantor. A personal financial statement lists a person's assets, debts, and net worth. Ask likely owners for a draft early, since gaps here slow everything after the letter of intent.


Eligibility rules changed during 2026, and[SBA SOP 50 10 8.1](https://www.sba.gov/document/sop-50-10-lender-development-company-loan-programs) took effect October 1, 2026. Confirm each buyer group against current guidance before you invest time. Our summary of[2026 SBA program changes](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-loan-program-changes-2026) covers what shifted.


#### Deal Size and Seller Financing Expectations


Bigger deals face deeper review under the lender due diligence rules in SOP 50 10 8.1. Initial acquisitions priced at $3 million or more need a Quality of Earnings (QoE) report plus a business valuation. A QoE is an independent accounting review that tests whether reported earnings are real and repeatable.


The lender must commission that valuation itself and may not use one prepared for the buyer or seller. Buyers at this size should expect more time and cost before closing.


Seller financing plays a smaller role than many buyers hope. In the[IBBA Market Pulse Q2 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/the-market-pulse-survey-q2-2026-reports-the-latest-trends-in-business-sales-up-to-50m-302858664.html) , seller financing accounted for less than 10% of most deals in Q2. The same survey of 255 brokers and M&A advisors found Main Street deals averaged six to 10 months from engagement to close.


A buyer counting on a large seller note or a 60-day close needs a reset now. Use this checklist to wrap up the financial screen.


Item What to ask for Why it matters


Proof of funds Recent bank or brokerage statements Confirms liquid cash on hand


Equity source A written breakdown of where the 10% comes from SBA 7(a) limits which sources count


Seller note terms Whether the seller will accept full standby Standby sources cap at half the injection


Personal financial statement A draft from each likely 20%+ owner Lenders collect one from every guarantor


Ownership chart Every owner and their percentage Shows who must sign a guaranty


Prequalification letter Any lender letter the buyer holds Shows a lender has done an early review


‍


### Screen Motivation and Experience


Cash alone does not make a qualified buyer. Motivation is the reason a buyer wants to own a business, and it shapes how they handle tough moments in diligence.


Start by sorting buyers into one of three groups:


- **Strategic buyers:** Companies that want to add your listing to a business they already run.
- **Financial buyers:** Investors, such as private equity groups, who buy for returns and often hire managers.
- **First-time buyers and searchers:** Individuals buying their first company, often with an SBA 7(a) loan.


A searcher is someone who runs a dedicated hunt for one business to buy and operate. Ask every buyer why now, and what happens if they do not buy this year. Vague answers often point to someone still exploring.


Next, match experience to the business. A buyer without industry background can still be a fit. Ask how they will fill the gap, such as keeping a key manager or hiring an operator.


‍


### Map Every Decision-Maker


A decision-maker is anyone who can approve, block, or fund the deal. Missing one late in the process can stall a signed letter of intent (LOI), a nonbinding offer that outlines price and terms.


Ask early who else must say yes:


- **Partners:** Co-buyers who share ownership and may cross the 20% guaranty line.
- **Spouses:** Family members whose household assets stand behind a personal guaranty.
- **Investors:** Outside backers who supply equity and may hold approval rights.
- **Advisors:** Accountants or attorneys whose sign-off the buyer is waiting on.


Get each person on at least one call before the LOI. A partner who stays silent now can become a "no" during underwriting.


‍


### Check Deal Fit and Realistic Expectations


Deal fit compares what the buyer wants with what you have to sell. Check industry, earnings range, geography, and deal structure against your current listings.


Many brokers talk about size in EBITDA, short for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. It is a common measure of operating profit. A buyer seeking $2 million in EBITDA with a small budget does not fit a Main Street listing.


Use the 10% equity floor as a quick math check. A buyer with $150,000 in qualifying equity supports a total project cost of about $1.5 million at most. If your listing needs more, the buyer needs more cash or a different target.


‍


### Prequalification vs. Preapproval


Buyers often mix up these terms, so define them in your process. Each one tells you something different:


- **Broker screen:** Your check of profile, funds, motivation, and fit before sharing the CIM.
- **Lender prequalification:** A lender's early estimate based on buyer-reported data and a soft credit pull.
- **Lender approval:** A credit decision made after full underwriting of the buyer and the business.


A soft pull is a credit check that does not affect the person's credit score. Approval, sometimes called preapproval, comes later in the[SBA loan process, step by step](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-loan-process-step-by-step-guide-prequalification-to-funding) , after document review and valuation.


A prequalification letter shows a lender's early interest. Proof of funds shows actual cash, so ask for both. Some brokers use[multi-lender marketplace platforms](https://www.lendflow.com/post/multi-lender-marketplace-platform) to get soft-pull prequalification from several lenders at once.


‍


### Score Buyers to Prioritize Your Pipeline


A buyer scoring system ranks buyers by readiness so you spend time on the strongest first. Use a simple A–D scale:


Tier Profile and motivation Financing readiness Next step


A Complete profile, signed NDA, clear reason to buy Verified funds covering 10%+ of project cost and a lender prequalification Share the CIM and schedule a seller call


B Complete profile with gaps in experience or decision-makers Funds shown, but the equity source is unclear Share the CIM after closing the gaps


C Broad criteria or an early-stage search No proof of funds yet Stay in touch and request documents


D Shifting story or slow replies Cannot show funds or relies on borrowed equity Pause and keep deal details private


Scores change over time. Re-check at key moments, such as before an LOI or when the buyer's capital or partners change.


‍


### Red Flags That Signal a Buyer Won't Close


One red flag is a reason to ask questions. Several together usually mean it is time to pause.


- **No proof of funds:** The buyer delays or refuses to share statements.
- **Borrowed equity:** The injection plan relies on borrowed money the lender may not accept.
- **Shifting criteria:** Industry, size, or budget changes every time you talk.
- **Slow responses:** Replies take days, and documents arrive late or incomplete.
- **Missing decision-makers:** A partner or investor stays out of every conversation.
- **Unrealistic terms:** The buyer expects a large seller note with payments or a very fast close.


‍

### FAQ


These quick answers cover the questions brokers and buyers ask most about buyer qualification.


#### What questions do brokers ask to qualify a buyer?


Brokers ask how much liquid cash the buyer has and where the equity injection comes from. They also ask why now, who else must approve, and what business fits.


#### Should buyers sign an NDA before prequalification?


A buyer can complete a profile and a basic financial screen first. They should sign an NDA before seeing the business name, financials, or CIM.


#### Is an SBA prequalification letter proof of funds?


No, a prequalification letter only shows a lender's early interest. Proof of funds is a statement that shows the buyer's actual cash.


#### How much cash does a buyer need for an SBA 7(a) acquisition loan?


Under SOP 50 10 8.1, an initial acquisition needs at least a 10% equity injection on total project cost. Standby seller debt and similar sources can cover no more than half of it.


#### What is a buyer scoring system?


A buyer scoring system ranks buyers in tiers, such as A through D. Tiers reflect financing readiness, motivation, decision authority, and deal fit.
